content.title: Convert Scanned Image to Text on iPhone
content.meta_description: Convert scanned images to text on your iPhone. Extract printed text offline with free on-device OCR, copy words instantly, or export as a text file.
content.h1: How to Convert a Scanned Image to Text on iPhone
content.quick_answer: To convert a scanned image to text, scan the printed page or select a photo in Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit. The app runs on-device OCR to detect characters automatically. You can then copy the extracted text straight to your clipboard or export it as a .txt file for free.
intro: You take a photo of a printed book page, reference sheet, or paper report, but typing paragraphs into an email or notes app takes too much time. You need to convert the image into digital, selectable text that you can edit immediately.

Your iPhone or iPad can read printed characters directly from an image without sending your private files across the internet. This guide explains how to extract printed text from scanned photos using on-device optical character recognition (OCR) and compares the workflow with built-in iOS tools.
For extracting cursive notes, see our dedicated guide on recognizing handwriting. If you need a fully formatted .docx file rather than raw text, refer to our walkthrough for converting PDF to Word.
content.steps_heading: How to Extract Text from an Image Using Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit

steps.title: Capture or import the page
steps.detail: Open the camera in Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit to photograph your physical document, or import an existing photo from your library. Automatic edge detection identifies the document borders in real time, cropping background clutter and straightening perspective so text lines lay flat.

steps.title: Clean up the image with enhancement filters
steps.detail: Inspect the captured frame for uneven lighting or shadows that might obscure words. Apply the Auto, Black & White, Grayscale, or Shadow Removal filter to create crisp contrast between printed letters and the paper background. Clean contrast prevents the OCR engine from misreading punctuation or letter shapes.

steps.title: Run on-device text recognition (OCR)
steps.detail: Trigger the text recognition feature on the processed image. The OCR engine reads the printed characters entirely on your device without uploading files to remote servers. The app generates selectable text directly from the scan.

steps.title: Copy the text or export as a .txt file
steps.detail: Review the recognized characters on your screen. You can select and copy the text directly to your clipboard for pasting into other apps, or export the full output as an unformatted .txt file at no charge.

content.alternatives_heading: Alternative Ways to Convert Images to Text on iOS

alternatives.method: Apple Live Text in Camera and Photos
alternatives.how: Open the photo in the iOS Photos app or point the native Camera at the document on iOS 15 or later. Tap the Live Text icon in the bottom corner to highlight text, then select, copy, translate, or look up words directly.
alternatives.best_for: Quickly grabbing a single sentence, paragraph, phone number, or email address from a clean photo without saving a separate text file.
alternatives.limitation: Requires iOS 15 and later on an iPhone XS/XR or newer. It lacks document cropping or dedicated filters to clean up low-contrast paper scans before processing.

alternatives.how: Upload your scanned PDF or image to Google Drive, tap the three dots or right-click, and choose Open with > Google Docs. The system creates a new document containing the original image followed by the extracted text.
alternatives.best_for: Converting printed pages when working primarily on a desktop browser within the Google ecosystem.
alternatives.limitation: Requires an internet connection and uploading your document to external servers. Original document formatting is often lost, and recognition quality suffers on low-contrast images.

content.features_heading: Key App Features for Converting Scanned Images to Text

feature_points.benefit: Extracts printed text directly from scanned pages so you can copy characters to your clipboard or export a clean .txt file without paying for a subscription.
Straightens angled camera shots and trims away desk backgrounds automatically, ensuring text lines are aligned horizontally for higher character-recognition accuracy.
Uses Black & White, Grayscale, and Shadow Removal filters to remove dark spots and brighten paper backgrounds, making printed text sharp enough for the OCR tool to decipher.
Executes character recognition locally on your iPhone hardware, ensuring sensitive scans never upload to third-party cloud servers during the conversion process.

tips: Position the document on a flat, contrasting surface so edge detection can crop cleanly around page borders without clipping text margins.
Avoid harsh overhead lights that cast phone or hand silhouettes across lines of print; read our guide on removing shadows from scanned documents if lighting defects linger.
Keep your camera parallel to the document to minimize distortion, allowing the OCR system to read baseline fonts without skewed perspective.
Clean your camera lens before scanning to avoid smudges that blur small punctuation marks, periods, and commas.

faqs.question: How do I extract printed text from a scanned image on iPhone?
faqs.answer: You can extract printed text by opening the document in Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit and running the on-device OCR tool. The app detects the printed words locally and lets you copy them immediately or export a .txt file. Alternatively, you can use iOS Live Text in the native Photos app if your iPhone supports it.

faqs.question: Can I convert printed document scans into text files without paying for a subscription?
faqs.answer: Yes. On-device OCR in Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit is a free feature. You can copy the extracted characters directly to your clipboard or export the content as a .txt file at no cost. If you need to convert handwriting rather than printed text, read our dedicated guide on handwritten notes at /ocr-handwriting-iphone.

faqs.question: How does Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit OCR compare to iOS Live Text?
faqs.answer: Live Text is built into iOS 15 and later on iPhone XS/XR and newer, letting you select and copy words inside Photos or Camera. Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit pairs OCR with automatic page cropping and contrast-enhancing filters, and exports the full transcription directly as a .txt file.

faqs.question: Does OCR work completely offline on my iPhone?
faqs.answer: Yes. The OCR engine in Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit processes text directly on your iPhone or iPad hardware. Your documents and extracted text remain stored on your device and are never uploaded to remote servers unless you select a cloud destination.

faqs.question: Why does OCR make mistakes on low-contrast or shadowed images?
faqs.answer: OCR engines rely on clean visual separation between dark letterforms and the lighter background. Shadows or faint print blur those edges, leading to misread characters. Using Black & White, Grayscale, or the Shadow Removal filter before running OCR clarifies letter boundaries.
